texts.orig: Use of pliers or other mechanical devices shall be prohibited, because that process can deform the insulation and change the characteristics of the wire. Wire insulation shall not be damaged by any manufacturing process. Once the contacts have been assembled, seat (in some cases install) the TPA (terminal position assurance). If a lubricant is desired, isopropyl alcohol shall be used. There shall not be a separation in the twisted pair (this is also referred to as an eye), where the wires do not maintain the factory twist, and open in the distance between the wires. During the heat shrink process, ensure that the adhesive does not get in between the wires. Separation of the wires will decrease signal quality, and will be rejected. That is why maintaining a factory twist, means that if there is a separation in the 2 wires (or an open eye), that this is cause for rejection. An example is shown below. Keeping the Ethernet twisted pair with mild bends will help to avoid the chance of sharp bends that will degrade Ethernet signal quality. Avoid practices that will make 1 wire longer than the other wire, such as a sharp bend directly behind the connector.

texts.orig: 10.7 Sealed Splice - Shall meet the following requirements. Perform the tests and track the results at a minimum of 1 time each 3 months. Document results shall available to Caterpillar upon request. The assumption is that each harness supplier will have a controlled, repeatable process documented that is repeatable. If the splice fails the water test, a new sample shall be used to validate process controls. If different size and combinations of wire are used, then tests shall be done to validate each wire combination and heat shrink seal.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 10.7.1 Water Immersion - One wire of the splice shall be connected to an air pressure source. The other wire ends shall be sealed. The center section of a sealed splice shall be immersed in tap water. 35 kPa of air pressure is applied for 120 seconds. Bubble formation for the first 60s is ignored as the test conditions become stable. After 60s, for the duration of the test, no air bubbles shall be visible.
texts.text: Water Immersion - One wire of the splice shall be connected to an air pressure source. The other wire ends shall be sealed. The center section of a sealed splice shall be immersed in tap water. 35 kPa of air pressure is applied for 120 seconds. Bubble formation for the first 60s is ignored as the test conditions become stable. After 60s, for the duration of the test, no air bubbles shall be visible.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 10.7.2 Insulation Resistance - Immerse the center section of a sealed splice in water containing 5 percent sodium chloride by weight. Measure the insulation resistance between one wire in the splice and the water after a 24 h immersion. The applied voltage shall be 100 VDC. The resistance shall be measured 60 s after the voltage is applied. The insulation resistance shall be greater than 10 megohms.
